words: فكيف تتقون يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they disbelieve, how can they shield themselves from God's punishment on a day whose terror makes children gray-haired?
rows.anchor: أي بأي شيء [تتحصنون] من عذاب الله في يوم من هوله يشيب فيه الصغير من غير كبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits because of that dreadful day.
rows.anchor: أي السماء تنشق به كما قال: (إذا السماء انشقت).

rows.speaker: قيل في التفسير
rows.claim: An interpretation reported in tafsir takes the phrase to mean that the sky is weighed down by God.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: (السماء منفطر به) أي السماء مثقلة بالله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative readings of ‘half’ and ‘a third,’ the phrase clearly explains the amount meant by ‘less than two-thirds.’
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (نصفه) بالنصب (وثلثه) فهو بين حسن. وهو تفسير مقدار قيامه

rows.speaker: قارئ
rows.claim: A reading with both ‘half’ and ‘a third’ conjoined means that you stand for less than half the night and less than a third of it.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ و (نصفه) و (ثلثه)، فالمعنى وتقوم أدنى من نصفه ومن ثلثه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form is possible in Arabic, but it cannot be read here because it conflicts with the consonantal text.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقرأ في هذا الموضع السماء منفطرة؛ لخلاف المصحف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine agreement can treat ‘sky’ as meaning ‘roof’; the verse elsewhere calls the sky a protected roof.
rows.anchor: أحدهما على معنى السماء معناه السقف، قال الله عز وجل: (وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine agreement can also be relational: ‘sky’ is understood as possessing a cleaving, as a nursing woman possesses nursing.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني على قوله: امرأة مرضع، أي على جهة النسب. المعنى السماء ذات انفطار، كما تقول امرأة مرضع أي ذات رضاع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can mean luxury or ease, and can also mean a beneficent favor from a person or a gracious act from God.
rows.anchor: النعمة التنعم، والنعمة اليد الجميلة عند الإنسان والصنع من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts the alternate vocalization because those favored by God may be believers or unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولو قرئت أولي النعمة لكان وجها، لأن المنعم عليهم يكونون مؤمنين وغير مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deeds sent ahead are better for you than the enjoyments of worldly life.
rows.anchor: معناه خيرا لكم من متاع الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Khayran’ is the second object of ‘find’; ‘huwa’ is a separator, and accusative is best in Arabic and required in the Qur'anic reading.
rows.anchor: و (خيرا) منصوب مفعول ثان ل (تجدوه) ودخلت " هو " فصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan.
rows.anchor: (مكية) بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قوله عز وجل: (يا أيها المدثر (1)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard geminated form contracts from ‘al-mutaddaththir’; a form retaining tāʾ is also transmitted, by the same contraction as ‘al-muzzammil.’
rows.anchor: القراءة بتشديد، والأصل المتدثر، والعلة فيها كالعلة في المتزمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-muddaththir’ has the same meaning as ‘al-muzzammil.’
rows.anchor: وتفسيرها كتفسير المزمل. وقد رويت المتدثر - بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ enters as the response to a conditional sense.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء على معنى جواب الجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnify your Lord by describing Him as exalted and greatest; the command means, ‘Rise and warn, and magnify your Lord.’
rows.anchor: المعنى قم فأنذر أي قم فكبر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is ‘do not be treacherous,’ since a treacherous person is called dirty in his garments.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكن غادرا. يقال للغادر دنس الثياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean purify yourself.
rows.anchor: ويكون (وثيابك فطهر) أي نفسك فطهر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to shorten the garment, keeping it from dragging on the ground and picking up impurity.
rows.anchor: وقيل (وثيابك فطهر) أي ثيابك فقصر لأن تقصير الثوب أبعد من النجاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with either kasra or ḍamma on rāʾ, and the two forms have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: بكسر الراء، وقرئت بضم الراء، ومعناهما واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to abandon worship of idols.
rows.anchor: وتأويلهما اهجر عبادة الأوثان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-rujz’ means punishment; the command then means to shun whatever leads to God's punishment.
rows.anchor: والرجز في اللغة العذاب، قال الله تعالى: (ولما وقع عليهم الرجز). فالتأويل على هذا ما يؤدي إلى عذاب الله فاهجره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not give something while expecting to receive something greater in return.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعط شيئا مقدرا أن تأخذ بدله ما هو أكثر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Tastakthiru’ is a circumstantial clause describing an anticipated state.
rows.anchor: وتستكثر حال متوقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This instruction is specific to the Prophet; others do not sin by gifting in hope of a larger return, while the Prophet was trained in the noblest manners.
rows.anchor: وهذا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خاصة وليس على الإنسان إثم أن يهدي هدية يرجو بها ما هو أكثر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make him undergo a severe hardship of punishment.
rows.anchor: أي سأحمله على مشقة من العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘qutila’ means ‘may he be cursed’; the same idiom occurs in 51:10.
rows.anchor: معنى - (قتل) ههنا لعن، ومثله: (قتل الخراصون (10).

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Al-Walid asks Meccan leaders what they will say about Muhammad when people ask, after noting the spread of his message.
rows.anchor: وكان الوليد بن المغيرة قال لرؤساء أهل مكة، قد رأيتم هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: When leaders propose calling Muhammad mad, al-Walid rejects it because anyone who spoke with him would recognize that he was not mad.
rows.anchor: قالوا نقول: هو مجنون، قال: إذن يخاطبوه فيعلموا أنه غير مجنون.

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: He rejects calling Muhammad a poet because Arabs know poetry and know his message is not poetry; he rejects ‘soothsayer’ because Muhammad says ‘if God wills.’
rows.anchor: قالوا: فنقول إنه كاهن، قال الكهنة لا تقول إنه يكون كذا وكذا إن شاء الله وهو يقول إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: After reflection, al-Walid calls Muhammad's message sorcery learned from Musaylima and the people of Babylon.
rows.anchor: ففكر وعبس وجهه وبسر، أي نظر بكراهة شديدة. فقال: ما هذا الذي أتى به محمد إلا سحر يأثره عن مسيلمة وعن أهل بابل.

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl tells his uncle that people say he has apostatized and that they plan to gather wealth for him in exchange for what he might take from Muhammad's followers.
rows.anchor: وجاء أبو جهل ابن أخيه، فقالوا: إن القوم يقولون إنك قد صبوت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid replies that they will never satisfy him, asks how he could take their money, and says he is among the wealthiest people.
rows.anchor: فقال: والله ما يشبعون، فكيف أقدر أن آخذ منهم مالا وإني لمن أيسر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means, ‘This is nothing but human speech.’
rows.anchor: أي ما هذا إلا قول البشر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Saqar’ is diptote because it is a feminine proper name.
rows.anchor: لا ينصرف لأنها معرفة، وهي مؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is one of the names of Hell.
rows.anchor: وسقر اسم من أسماء جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks what could make you know what Saqar is.
rows.anchor: تأويله وما أعلمك أي شيء سقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-bashar’ is the plural of ‘bashara’; Saqar burns the skin until it turns black.
rows.anchor: البشر جمع بشرة، أي تحرق الجلد حتى يسود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nineteen are angels assigned over Saqar, described elsewhere as stern, mighty angels who obey God.
rows.anchor: أي على سقر تسعة عشر ملكا، ووصفهم الله في موضع آخر فقال: (عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading has fatḥa on the ʿayn; a sukūn reading is attributed to easing the many successive vowels in a compound numeral built on fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئت بتسكين العين، والقراءة بفتحها، وإنما أسكنها من أسكنها لكثرة الحركات، وذلك أنهما اسمان جعلا اسما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the numeral with inflection according to its original components, but this is grammatically rare; the built form on fatḥa is best.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم تسعة عشر فأعربت على الأصل، وذلك قليل في النحو، والأجود تسعة عشر على البناء على الفتح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They said that a sinner among the Children of Israel would find his sin written on his door the next morning, and asked why they could not receive the same.
rows.anchor: قيل كانوا يقولون: كان من أذنب من بني إسرائيل يجد ذنبه مكتوبا من غد على بابه فما بالنا لا نكون كذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an explains their demand elsewhere: they would not believe until a book was sent down for them to read.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في القرآن تفسير طلبهم في سورة بني إسرائيل في قوله: (ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy of having His punishment feared and of having people do what leads to His forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أي هو أهل أن يتقى عقابه، وأهل أن يعمل بما يؤدي إلى مغفرته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan.
rows.anchor: (مكية) بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قوله عز وجل: (لا أقسم بيوم القيامة (1)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone agrees that ‘lā uqsim’ means ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection.’
rows.anchor: لا اختلاف بين الناس أن معناه أقسم بيوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take ‘lā’ as redundant despite standing at the sūra's opening, because the Qur'an is continuous like one sūra; they compare ‘li-allā yaʿlama ahlu al-kitāb.’
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم " لا " لغو وإن كانت في أول السورة، لأن القرآن كله كالسورة الواحدة

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians take ‘lā’ as a rebuttal to deniers of resurrection: ‘No, it is not as you claim; I swear by the Day of Resurrection.’
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحوبين: " لا " رد لكلامهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement ‘you will be resurrected’ supplies the answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: أقسم بيوم القيامة وقوله: (إنكم مبعوثون) دل على الجواب

words: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is, ‘Yes, We shall gather you, being able to restore even your fingertips as they were.’
rows.anchor: المعنى: بلى لنجمعنكم قادرين، المعنى أقسم بيوم القيامة والنفس اللوامة لنجمعنها قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه.

rows.speaker: جاء في التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsir says the fingertips could be made like a camel's hoof.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير بلى نقدر على أن نجعله كخف البعير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the reading that God gathers the bones and can restore even the small fingertip bones to their original form after decay.
rows.anchor: والذي هو أشكل بجمع العظام بلى نجمعها قادرين، على تسوية بنانه على ما كانت، وإن قل عظامها وصغرت وبلغ منها البلى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife every soul reproaches its owner: for evil deeds if they were bad, and for not doing more if they were good.
rows.anchor: أن كل نفس تلوم صاحبها في الآخرة إن كان عمل شرا لامته نفسه وأن كان عمل خيرا لامته على ترك الاستكثار منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces are radiant from the bliss of Paradise and look toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: نضرت بنعيم الجنة والنظر إلى ربها. قال الله - عز وجل -: (تعرف في وجوههم نضرة النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Bāsira’ describes faces that are ugly and scowling, certain that punishment is coming.
rows.anchor: (باسرة) كريهة مقطبة، قد أيقنت بأن العذاب نازل بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘tazunnu’ means to be certain, and ‘fāqira’ is a calamity of punishment.
rows.anchor: توقن أن يفعل بها داهية من العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Kallā’ is a rebuke and warning: desist from what leads to punishment.
rows.anchor: (كلا) ردع وتنبيه، ومعناه ارتدعوا عما يؤدي إلى العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reminds people of the first hardship of the Hereafter, when the soul reaches the collarbones.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم الله بصعوبة أول أيام الآخرة عند بلوغ النفس الترقوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the moment of distress, someone asks who can heal this state, meaning who can perform an incantation to rescue the dying.
rows.anchor: أي من يشفي من هذه الحال، وهذا - والله أعلم - يقوله القائل عند البأس، أي من يقدر أن يرقي من الموت.

rows.speaker: قيل في التفسير
rows.claim: Another interpretation asks who will carry the soul upward: the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: (من راق) من يرقى بروحه أملائكة الرحمة أم ملائكة العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person whose soul reaches the collarbones realizes that he is leaving this world.
rows.anchor: وأيقن الذي تبلغ روحه إلى تراقيه أنه مفارق للدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, one leg clings to the other.
rows.anchor: عند الموت تلتصق الساق بالساق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation joins the final hardship of worldly life to the first hardship of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قيل والتفت آخر شدة الدنيا بأول شدة الآخرة.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: ‘Aqbarahu’ means to provide someone a grave, whereas ‘qabartuhu’ means to bury him; an unnamed poet uses ‘qābir’ for the one who buries.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها. . . عاش ولم ينقل إلى قابر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: ‘Ansharahu’ means God raised the dead, who then rise; an unnamed poet witnesses the usage ‘al-mayyit al-nāshir.’
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا. . . يا عجبا للميت الناشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should consider how God created their food and the food of all animals as a means of their lives.
rows.anchor: أي فلينظر الإنسان كيف خلق الله طعامه وطعام جميع الحيوان الذي جعله الله سببا لحياتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ‘innā,’ the clause begins independently; with ‘annā,’ it is an apposition to ‘food’ and is in the genitive position.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (إنا) فعلى الابتداء والاستئناف ومن قرأ (أنا) فعلى البدل من الطعام، ويكون (إنا) في موضع جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God split the earth by means of vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي بالنبات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ḥabb’ covers everything harvested, such as wheat and barley, and other grain used for food.
rows.anchor: والحب كل ما حصد، كالحنطة والشعير وكل ما يتغذى به من ذي حب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Qaḍb’ means fresh, tender fodder.
rows.anchor: والقضب الرطبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ḥadāʾiq’ is the plural of ‘ḥadīqa,’ meaning orchards with dense, interwoven trees.
rows.anchor: حدائق واحدتها حديقة، وهي البساتين، والشجر الملتف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ghulban’ means thickly grown and large.
rows.anchor: قوله (غلبا) معناه متكاثفة عظام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Abb’ means all pasture that livestock feed on.
rows.anchor: الأب جميع الكلأ الذي تعتلفه الماشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs show God's oneness through the creation of nourishment for every kind of animal.
rows.anchor: وذكر الله عز وجل من آياته ما يدل على وحدانيته في إنشاء ما يغذو جميع الحيوان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The records are opened and each person receives a book in the right or left hand according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: ونشرت. نشرت الصحف وأعطى كل إنسان كتابه بيمينه أو بشماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read ‘kushitat’ or ‘qushitat’; both mean stripped away or pulled off, as one pulls off a roof.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (قشطت) بالقاف، ومعناهما قلعت كما يقلع السقف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāf and qāf often substitute for one another; ‘labaktu’ and ‘labaqtu’ both mean that I mixed something.
rows.anchor: والقاف والكاف تبدل إحداهما من الأخرى كثيرا. ومثل ذلك لبكت الشيء ولبقته إذا خلطته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with or without gemination; both mean ‘kindled,’ though the geminated form means kindled repeatedly.
rows.anchor: و (سعرت) بالتشديد والتخفيف، ومعناه أوقدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: أي قربت من المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A soul knew what it had brought’ is the answer to the preceding events.
rows.anchor: أي قربت من المتقين، وجواب هذه الأشياء قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When those events occur on Resurrection Day, every soul knows its deeds and is recompensed according to them.
rows.anchor: علمت في ذلك الوقت كل نفس ما أحضرت، أي من عمل، فأثيبت على قدر عملها.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the divine attributes as meaning ‘possessor of mercy.’
rows.anchor: معناه فيما ذكر أبو عبيدة: ذو الرحمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern faʿlān intensifies a quality, as ‘ghaḍbān’ means filled with anger; ‘raḥmān’ describes mercy encompassing everything and is reserved for God.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان ذلك لأن بناء فعلان من أبنية ما يبالغ في وصفه، ألا ترى أنك إذا قلت غضبان فمعناه الممتلئ غضبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God's mercy encompasses everything, ‘al-Raḥmān’ may not be used of anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: فرحمن الذي وسعت رحمته كل شي فلا يجوز أن يقال لغير الله رحمن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two attributes are genitive because they praise God and follow the grammatical case of His name.
rows.anchor: وخفضت هذه الصفات لأنها ثناء على الله - عز وجل - فكان إعرابها إعراب اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In non-Qur'anic speech, ‘rabb al-ʿālamīn’ may be genitive as a continuation or accusative as praise, with an implied ‘I mention the Lord of the worlds.’
rows.anchor: فمن نصب رب العالمين فإنما ينصب لأنه ثناء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative construction means ‘I mention the Lord of the worlds’; the nominative construction means ‘He is the Lord of the worlds.’
rows.anchor: فقوله: رب العالمين - كأنه قال أذكر رب العالمين، وإذا قال رب العالمين فهو على قولك: هو رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line illustrates that accusative participles may follow a preceding noun or be accusatives of praise, while nominative forms can state ‘they are the ones’; the grammarians accept the listed case combinations.
rows.anchor: الطاعنين ولما يظعنوا أحدا. . . والقائلين لمن دار نخليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although nominative and accusative forms are possible in ordinary speech, the Qur'an uses the best and most eloquent wording, ‘rabb al-ʿālamīn al-raḥmān al-raḥīm.’
rows.anchor: قد فسرنا أنه لا يجوز في القرآن إلا (رب العالمين الرحمن الرحيم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-ʿālamīn’ means everything God created, as in ‘He is Lord of everything.’
rows.anchor: معناه كل ما خلق الله، كما قال؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-ʿālamīn’ is the plural of ‘ʿālam’; the word has no singular from its own form because it gathers different kinds, while a singular ‘ʿālam’ would gather members of one kind.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع عالم، تقول: هؤلاء عالمون، ورأيت عالمين، ولا واحد لعالم من لفظه لأن عالما جمع لأشياء مختلفة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says the plural nūn is opened to distinguish it from the dual nūn, which is kasra.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أنها فتحت ليفرق بينها وبين نون الإثنين، تقول: هذان عالمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural nūn is also opened at a meeting of two still letters; kasra is avoided as heavy after wāw or yāʾ, as in the cited forms ‘sawfa’ and ‘ayna Zayd.’
rows.anchor: وكذلك نون الجماعة فتحت لالتقاء الساكنين، ولم تكسر لثقل الكسرة بعد الواو والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading ‘mālik’ follows grammatically from ‘al-ḥamdu lillāh.’
rows.anchor: القراءة الخفض على مجرى الحمد لله مالك يوم الدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative is possible in ordinary speech by analogy with ‘rabb al-ʿālamīn’ and ‘al-raḥmān al-raḥīm,’ but he does not favor it as a Qur'anic reading.
rows.anchor: وإن نصب - في الكلام - على ما نصب عليه (رب العالمين والرحمن الرحيم) جاز في الكلام. فأما في القراءة فلا أستحسنه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary speech the phrase can also be accusative as a vocative, ‘O Lord of the worlds, O Master of the Day of Judgment,’ praising God after ‘praise belongs to God.’
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن تنصب رب العالمين ومالك يوم الدين على النداء في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both ‘mālik’ (owner) and ‘malik’ (king) are recited.
rows.anchor: وقرئ (ملك يوم الدين، ومالك يوم الدين).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is singled out because creatures are then compelled to acknowledge that all sovereignty belongs to God and that none can benefit or harm another.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص يوم الدين والله عز وجل يملك كل شيء لأنه اليوم الذي يضطر فيه المخلوقون إلى أن يعرفوا أن الأمر كله لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ‘mālik’ accords with the declaration, ‘Whose is the sovereignty today?’ and is like asking who owns sovereignty today.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (مالك يوم الدين) فعلى قوله (لمن الملك اليوم). وهو بمنزلة من المالك اليوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ‘malik’ means the possessor of a kingdom on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (ملك يوم الدين) فعلى معنى " ذو المملكة " في يوم الدين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: One report attributes the reading ‘malik yawm al-dīn’ to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها قراءة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -.
